game: Week 6 BAL@CLE, kickoff not in pack / CLE +3 (BAL -3), implied BAL 21.25 CLE 18.25 / total 39.5 / weather not saved

script.base: A one-score, run-leaning 39.5 game. BAL leads or is tied late and keeps feeding Derrick Henry (74 carries, 264 yards over weeks 3-5) without shutting the pass game off, because that same window already produced Zay Flowers 25 targets and 255 yards. CLE stays competitive behind Quinshon Judkins (49/167) and Deshaun Watson's 20 designed/scramble carries, with Denzel Boston (19 targets, 303 air yards) as the shot-play, not a shootout.
script.flip1: BAL gets up two scores early, Henry's carry count spikes, Flowers and Mark Andrews targets stall, and CLE abandons Judkins so Boston, Harold Fannin and K.C. Concepcion volume rises while Watson's rushes turn into sacks or empty-set dropbacks.
script.flip2: Home dog CLE leads late. BAL throws more (Flowers and Rashod Bateman live, Henry under 90.5 dies) while BAL's 3.98 YPC run defense and 32% blitz keep the total from becoming a shootout.

injury_fallout: No injury report, practice status, or inactives in the pack, so no confirmed next-man-up. Lamar Jackson still has 8/70 rushing over the same L3 as Tyler Huntley 7/40, so this is not a Huntley-starts spot. CLE's L3 rushers are Judkins 49/167, Watson 20/111, Raheim Sanders 6/38, Bojorquez 1/0 — Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime have posted props but no L3 carries, so they are not the backfield. Jerry Jeudy is already down to 10 targets versus Boston 19, Fannin 18 and Concepcion 18; that is a role fact, not an injury inference. Re-check final inactives; none are in this pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Location splits only: CLE allows middle 9.38 YPA (32 att) versus left 6.53 (68) and right 6.15 (74). BAL allows middle 7.97 (35) versus left 6.88 (67) and right 6.52 (69).
matchup.pressure: CLE blitzes 25%. BAL QB EPA/dropback is 0.25 vs blitz (n=57) and 0.22 clean, so pressure does not suppress this offense. BAL blitzes 32%. CLE QB EPA is 0.05 vs blitz (n=70) and 0.06 clean — flat, no blitz bonus, and pressure that gets home would cut Watson rush yards into sacks and cut Boston's deep yards.
matchup.bleeds: CLE run defense bleeds: 4.64 YPC allowed and 20 runs of 10+ in 5 games, versus BAL 3.98 YPC and 13 runs of 10+. CLE's pass leak is the middle (9.38), not the outside. Explosive passes are similar: CLE 17 of 191, BAL 16 of 183.
matchup.overlap: Flowers is BAL's primary target (25 tgt, 255 rec yds, 176 air) into the only soft CLE zone, the middle. Henry's 24.7 carries/game overlap the soft CLE run defense, but his own 3.57 YPC sits under the 90.5 rung. Boston's 303 air yards overlap BAL's 16 explosives of 20+, but BAL's 32% blitz is the wrong pressure look for a 15.9 air-yards-per-target profile.

form: Weeks 3-5 only, no per-game split in the pack. Flowers 25/255/176 = 85.0 rec yds/g and 10.2 yards per target, air yards support it (58.7 air/g). Henry 74/264 = 88.0 rush yds/g at 3.57 YPC, 5 targets for 24 rec yds. Justice Hill 10/109 (10.9 YPC) is a long-play fluke on 3.3 carries/g; 7 targets, 27 rec yds (9.0/g). Andrews 18/79/109 = 26.3 rec yds/g, 4.4 YPT. Bateman 11/145/115 = 48.3/g on only 3.7 targets — explosive, cannot prove it wasn't one bomb. Watson 20/111 = 37.0 rush yds/g at 5.55 YPC. Boston 19/176/303 = 58.7/g. Fannin 18/82/140 = 27.3/g. Concepcion 18/78/101 = 26.0/g. Jeudy 10/55/85 = 18.3/g. Huntley 7/40 = 13.3 rush yds/g.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Flowers is already the Ravens' primary receiver at 85 yards a game on 25 targets over the last three, and 58.5 is a low rung against the defense that leaks the middle at 9.38 yards per attempt.
edge_players.must_be_true: Jackson plays, Flowers keeps a full route share near 8 targets, and the game does not become a pure Henry clock-kill after halftime. The 85-versus-58.5 cushion already coexisted with 74 Henry carries.
edge_players.kills_it: BAL leads by multiple scores early, Henry takes 25-plus carries, and Flowers is held to about 4 targets and finishes in the low 40s. Also killed by a late inactive or a wind report this pack does not have.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Watson has a real rushing role, 20 carries for 111 yards (37 a game) over the last three, and 30.5 sits under that number even though Baltimore has been the stingier run defense at 3.98 YPC.
edge_players.must_be_true: Watson starts, keeps about 6-7 rush attempts, and BAL's 32% blitz creates scramble yards instead of sacks in a one-score game.
edge_players.kills_it: The blitz gets home and those plays are sacks, or CLE trails big, empties the backfield, and Judkins plus dropbacks replace the designed runs.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so this is an L3-role check only. Flowers 85.0 versus 58.5 agrees by 26.5 yards. Watson 37.0 versus 30.5 agrees by 6.5 yards. Henry rush over 90.5 was a real script/matchup idea (CLE 4.64 YPC, 20 runs of 10+) but L3 is 88.0, a lean that the raw number disagrees with, so it is dropped not flagged. Hill rush over 12.5 is dropped as a 10.9 YPC fluke on 10 carries. Bateman 48.3 versus 19.5 cannot be split by game. Fannin under 36.5 and Boston over 50.5 lose to the pressure rule: BAL blitzes 32%, which boosts TE/checkdowns and kills deep yards. No model probability to distrust.

market_rung_price: zayflowers recyds over 58.5 -113; deshaunwatson rushyds over 30.5 -113.5. Main rungs only; no alt rungs and no no-vig in the pack. Do not use +nan prices (Concepcion, Andrews, Estime, McLaughlin rush+rec).
pre_mortem: It's Monday and both legs lost because BAL led by two scores at half, Henry took the clock, and Flowers saw four targets into a middle that Cleveland finally closed — that 9.38 YPA was only 32 attempts and there is no shell chart here. Watson missed 30.5 because the 32% blitz became sacks, not scrambles, once CLE emptied out, and two stuffed series erase a 6.5-yard cushion against a 3.98 YPC rush defense. No weather, no inactives, and no per-game split were in the pack, so wind or a snap limit would have been invisible. That counter is as loud as the Watson read, which is why he is only a lean and the first cut; it is not stronger than the Flowers cushion, so Flowers stays.
slip_story: One-score competitive script, not a blowout clock-kill and not a shootout. Flowers over is the BAL chain-mover leg that already hit alongside 74 Henry carries; Watson rush over is the CLE stay-in-it QB-run leg. They lose together if BAL blows it open. Do not add Boston/Fannin overs, a total under, or Henry — those need the trailing-shootout flip, the slog flip, or the lean that L3 already disagrees with.
